title: AMLA publishes report on cooperation in AML/CFT supervisory colleges

paras.text: The report draws on AMLA's participation in 17 AML/CFT college meetings and provides an overview of how these colleges operate in practice. It identifies good practices observed across colleges, as well as areas where cooperation and information exchange could be further strengthened.
The report finds that colleges generally operate in a manner proportionate to the risk profile of supervised entities and play an important role in supporting cross-border supervisory cooperation.
At the same time, it highlights opportunities to improve the timeliness of information sharing, strengthen risk-focused discussions and enhance the coordination of follow-up actions.
The findings have informed AMLA's ongoing work on the Regulatory Technical Standards on AML/CFT colleges and on its methodology for selecting and participating in colleges.
